card_roles.text:
Proof spine: measurement covariance excess N=V-V_q is positive and exactly zero between disjoint supports, preserving long-range quantum correlations; overlap counting bounds its row sums. The established Brooks-Harris inequality bounds V_q-C by beta/12 times the thermal double commutator. Support/weighted-strength Schur counting gives W<=4g k(k+ell)Delta I. Gibbs response Cov(Y,score)=-beta C and a Schur complement transfer covariance to actual information. C(C+R)^(-1)C-(C-R)=R(C+R)^(-1)R>=0 needs no commutation. These ingredients are credited prior work; the assembled theorem and its priority remain unreviewed. The main proof uses no Gaussian locality or covariance-floor lemma from N711.

For u with ||u||_2^2=O(n), additional optimal quantum readout information is at most O(n). If u^T F_Q u/||u||^2 diverges with beta,g,k,ell,Delta,eta fixed, the local/optimal information ratio tends to one; enhanced scaling itself is not guaranteed. With f=u dot Y, v=Var(f), q=||u||^2, (v-nu q)_+<=u^T C u<=v. Thus beta^2(v-nu q)_+^2/v<=u^T F_loc u<=u^T F_Q u<=beta^2 v, lower endpoint zero if v=0. The same variance gives static-susceptibility bounds. The scalar sample mean is asymptotically competitive at enhanced response, with the displayed locally unbiased estimator requiring separately acquired reference mean and slope; finite-displacement bias is outside its variance formula.

Acquisition: |f|<=L_u=(3/eta)^k||u||_1. Paired independent samples Z=(f_1-f_2)^2/2 estimate v; M>=2 L_u^4 zeta^(-2) log(2/p) pairs suffice for additive variance error zeta at failure p. Each copy costs n actual single-qubit measurements and O(n+km) arithmetic; streaming scalar processing is possible. Independent Gibbs preparation, equilibration, calibration, preparation bias, correlated sampling, model/temperature/strength verification and global fitting remain separate costs. The theorem supplies no inexpensive Gibbs sampler or efficient global likelihood optimizer.

Failures delimit the theorem: a single common detector flip bit on a low-temperature mean-field commuting family keeps positive marginal visibility but loses Omega(n^2) Fisher information. A one-qubit H=xX+zZ example has an indefinite observed negative-log-likelihood Hessian despite positive covariance. Independent maximally mixed Z-field qubits have fixed-readout loss proportional to n. Positive additive protection does not prevent a poorly conditioned direction from remaining poorly conditioned.

Only the all-directions corollary depends on the unreviewed N711 floor: if, in its exact original bounded-incidence setting, C>=c I with c=exp[-C_(k,Delta)(1+beta g)^2], then F_loc>=[c/(c+nu)] beta^2 C>=[c/(c+nu)] F_Q. This is a conditional scoped transfer, not a dependency of the main readout result or independent validation of N711.
